node_definition.done_when: Per §82 of the plan: the empty needs-you line (yours: N working · nothing needs you) is never printed; the needs-you line prints only when its set is non-empty and has changed, and on the reminder cadence while it stays non-empty; the settle line prints only when its tail names outstanding runs, and a drained settle prints nothing while the follower still exits with its settle code; the docstrings of reckon/crew/needs_you.py and the follower's summary code state the rule that a printed line names something the coordinator can act on. Fake-clock tests find: a set going from one unpromoted run to empty prints nothing; a drained settle prints nothing and the follower exits with the settle code; a settle with an outstanding run prints its line naming the run; a change in a non-empty set prints as now. Every test file under tests/ importing reckon.crew.needs_you or reckon.crew_follow_commands, rebuilt from the head tree, adds no failure against a base arm, both arms from git checkouts under the run's own scratch directory with RECKON_SESSION_HOST_SETTLE, RECKON_FOLLOWER_OWNER, RECKON_FOLLOWER_IMAGE_COMMIT and RECKON_FOLLOWER_SOURCE_ROOT unset, run in place on the fleet node with pytest -n 8; any id failing in one arm only is run five times alone in each arm. tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py passes at head. Every log is under the run directory, starts with its revision and the literal command, and ends in EXIT=. ruff check and ruff format --check add no findings on the changed files, judged against the base blobs.
